entities.summary:
Nike, Inc. is an American multinational footwear and apparel corporation founded in 1964 as Blue Ribbon Sports by Bill Bowerman and Phil Knight, rebranded as Nike in 1971. The world's largest supplier of athletic shoes and apparel, Nike's 'Just Do It' campaign and celebrity endorsement strategy transformed sports marketing globally.

Bill Bowerman's waffle-iron shoe sole innovation produced better traction for runners, while Phil Knight's business acumen drove distribution. The 1984 signing of Michael Jordan for the Air Jordan line was the most consequential endorsement in sports history, creating a $5 billion annual business and redefining celebrity brand partnerships. Nike's subsequent endorsements of Tiger Woods, Serena Williams, Cristiano Ronaldo, and LeBron James made it the dominant sports marketing company globally.

Nike's outsourcing of manufacturing to Asia — Vietnam, Indonesia, and China — while keeping design, marketing, and branding in Oregon became a business school case study in separating manufacturing from brand value. The 1990s sweatshop controversies sparked the modern labor rights movement in global supply chains. Nike's self-described status as a 'marketing company that happens to sell shoes' shifted emphasis from product to narrative — changing how corporations across all industries approach branding and culture.
